key_step: Apply the king property $x\to-x$ so the two exponential weights sum to 1, then integrate $x^3+x$.
justification: King property with an odd exponent on a symmetric interval is a single familiar move; the modulus of an even function and a polynomial integral add no real difficulty. Nearest anchor 2026-P2-Q4 (L1, king property on 1/(3^x+3)).

key_step: Differentiate with Leibniz, factor into five simple roots and read maxima/minima from sign changes of $f'$.
justification: Three routine steps (Leibniz, factoring, sign scheme) with no insight, hence L2 rather than L1; counting minima at $x=-2,0,2$ requires care but options help. Similar to 2021-P2-Q9 (L2, extrema from signs of a product).

key_step: Differentiate the integral equation twice and evaluate at $\cos x=1/\sqrt3$.
justification: Two applications of Leibniz rule with chain rule and a careful value substitution; routine chain, no unfamiliar idea, options available. Nearest anchor 2023-P2-Q1 (L3, differentiate an integral equation and solve a linear DE) which has an extra DE stage, so one level lower.

key_step: Partition $(0,1]$ by $[1/x]=n$ and sum $\sum 7^{-n}(1/n-1/(n+1))$ using the $-\ln(1-r)$ series.
justification: Needs the infinite partition, the telescoping-style split into two logarithmic series with an index shift, and exact algebra; the series idea is less drilled than standard integrals. Option format helps a little, so L3 against 2021-P2-Q19 (L4, greatest integer breakpoints in numerical format).

key_step: Find where the parabola crosses the integers $0,-1,-2$ and integrate the step function piece by piece.
justification: Routine but multi-piece computation with one irrational breakpoint $\frac{3+\sqrt{17}}{8}$; no insight beyond reading the graph, and the options allow a check. Easier than 2021-P2-Q19 (L4, numerical greatest-integer integral), so L2.

key_step: Recognise $f'\sec t+f\sec t\tan t$ as $(f\sec t)'$ and evaluate the limit by L'Hopital.
justification: One recognition (exact derivative) followed by a routine $0/0$ limit; the product-rule recognition is standard. Nearest anchor 2024-P2-Q16 (L3, king property plus an integral of a given function), which is a step heavier.
The pattern f(x)+f(x+k)=c is a standard coaching result: two linked steps (period, integral over a period) then counting periods. No heavy computation. Between 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) and 2023-P2-Q1 (L3).

key_step: Identify the running maximum of the cubic, then count non-differentiable points over five pieces including a greatest-integer jump.
justification: Several concepts chained: running max, greatest integer, continuity vs differentiability at four breakpoints (3 is continuous but has a kink, 5 is a jump), then an integral. Precision risk is real, though options exist. Nearest 2024-P2-Q13 (L4, piecewise function with a derived zero count, numerical).

key_step: Freeze $[x/2]$ on $[0,2),[2,4),[4,5]$ and integrate three cosines to zero.
justification: Three-block splitting with a sign change from the integer shift; each integral is elementary. A routine chain with no unfamiliar idea; harder than a one-line king-property question (2026-P2-Q4, L1).

key_step: Notice the two integrals are constants, so $f$ is linear, and solve the 2x2 moment system.
justification: Standard integral-equation setup with two constants and a small linear system; routine chain, no insight beyond recognising constants. One level below 2023-P2-Q1 (L3), which adds a differential equation.
